# Spatia

> Spatia is a free, local-first infinite canvas for organizing ideas, notes, files, and projects visually. One unbounded space where notes, text, shapes, frames, files and links live side by side — instead of pages and scrolling documents.

## What Spatia is

Spatia is a visual workspace, often described as an "infinite canvas" or spatial organizer. It is designed for thinking in space: place any idea anywhere, connect related items, and zoom from a bird's-eye overview of the whole workspace down to a single note. The closest mental models are an endless whiteboard, a mind-mapping surface, and a note app that does not force an order.

## Key facts

- Pricing: free to use. No account is required.
- Platforms: Windows 10 / 11 (x64) desktop app, Linux (x64) desktop app, plus a Web app / installable PWA that runs in any modern browser on desktop, phones, iPads and tablets.
- Storage: local-first. Desktop projects are saved as files on your machine; the Web app stores projects in your browser. Nothing is uploaded to a Spatia cloud.
- Offline: the desktop app works fully offline; the Web app works offline once loaded.
- Current version: 0.5.3.
- Source: Spatia is open source under the MIT License; the source code is available at https://github.com/SpatiaLabs/Spatia.
- Native scope: there is no separate iOS or Android native app — phones, iPads and tablets use the Web version.

## Product capabilities

- Infinite canvas with zoom and pan, a minimap, focus, and isolation modes.
- Objects: sticky notes, text, images, files, links, frames, seven built-in shapes, groups, and freehand pen strokes.
- Rich text in notes and text: bold, italic, underline, inline code, links, headings, bullets and numbered lists — lightweight inline markup stored as plain text.
- Connection lines and arrows that follow objects as they move or resize, with three routing styles — Curved (default), Elbow (orthogonal) and Bracket. Connections support branching: one object can fan out to many targets and many sources can converge into one, and the chosen route style is saved with the file.
- A grouped tools panel (Menu / sidebar) organized into clear sections with consistent icons and inline keyboard-shortcut hints; fully keyboard accessible and identical on desktop and web.
- Freehand pen with real-time ink, a stabilizer, stylus pressure support, and a partial or whole-stroke eraser.
- Seven distinct brush types (Pen, Pencil, Ballpoint, Marker, Brush, Highlighter, Calligraphy) with per-brush width/opacity response, texture and caps; the Calligraphy nib varies width with stroke direction. Brush type is saved with the stroke and with presets.
- A single layout-aware keyboard shortcut system (works the same on QWERTY, AZERTY and other layouts), plus full game-controller support (pan, zoom, drawing, selection, undo/redo and the command palette).
- Eight starter templates: blank, brainstorming, project planning, mind map, study, notes, product planning, personal.
- Search, tags, projects, folders, and version history with automatic snapshots.
- Import Markdown, OPML, FreeMind (.mm), Excalidraw (.excalidraw), and Miro board JSON — files convert to native objects on the canvas.
- Export to PNG, JPEG, PDF, Markdown, and the native .spatia / .spatia.json format.
- Plugin system: manifest-based, sandboxed, with a permissions and events API, including hosted plugins.
- Real-time collaboration with zero setup on the desktop — click Share and the local server starts automatically. Rooms survive server restarts and reconnect automatically. Synchronization uses targeted operation sync with last-writer-wins convergence.

## Frequently asked questions

- Where do my projects live? Desktop: in the files you save. Web app: in your browser's local storage.
- Does Spatia need an account? No.
- Can I export my work? Yes — PNG, JPEG, PDF, Markdown, and .spatia / .spatia.json.
- Is there a macOS or Linux desktop app? The desktop app targets Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x64; the Web app runs in any modern browser.
- Is Spatia open source? Yes. Spatia is released under the MIT License; the source code is available at https://github.com/SpatiaLabs/Spatia.
